decision: IV Glucose (Hypoglycaemia) › IMCI Chart 10 · 2 ml/kg of 10% glucose › ⚠ Never give undiluted 50% dextrose
fragment: Never give undiluted 50% dextrose to neonates or young children — risk of osmotic injury, hyperglycaemia, and intracerebral haemorrhage. Always dilute to ≤ 12.5% for a peripheral IV.

decision: Severe Dehydration (Emergency) › IMCI Chart 11 · 70 ml/kg RL · then ORS › Evidence notes

decision: Tuberculosis › 4.7.2 · Xpert Ultra · HRZE · 4-mo nonsevere › Investigations
fragment: Xpert Ultra (Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra) is now the initial diagnostic test for every child with presumed TB — not only when MDR-TB or HIV-associated TB is suspected. It is far more sensitive than the original Xpert and also detects rifampicin resistance. decision: Severe Dehydration (Plan C) › 5.2.1 · rapid IV rehydration · Table 13 › Which IV fluid
fragment: Ringer's lactate (Hartmann's) is preferred over 0.9% saline — balanced crystalloids give shorter hospital stays, better acid-base correction and less hypokalaemia (2023 Cochrane review). Use 0.9% saline only if Ringer's lactate is unavailable. Do NOT use 5% glucose (dextrose) or 0.18% saline with 5% dextrose — they raise the risk of hyponatraemia and cerebral oedema.

decision: Uncomplicated Malaria › P. vivax, ovale & malariae › Radical cure of P. vivax** (kills liver hypnozoites) — an **8-aminoquinoline**, dosed to region:
fragment: Primaquine 0.5 mg/kg/day for 14 days is the target here (range 0.25–0.5; total 3.5–7 mg/kg). The higher end is preferred for radical cure in East Africa, and is required for fast-relapsing strains in East Asia and Oceania. A 7-day course (0.5 mg/kg/day) may be used if G6PD activity ≥ 70%.

decision: Anorexia, Nausea & Vomiting › 8.7.2 · small frequent feeds · ondansetron › Metoclopramide — corrected dose
fragment: If metoclopramide is used (alternative only): 0.1–0.15 mg/kg (max 10 mg) every 6–8 h. decision: Osteomyelitis › 9.5.2 · cloxacillin / ceftriaxone · 3–4 wk · early oral switch › Treatment
fragment: Duration — much shorter than before: total 3–4 weeks for uncomplicated disease. Give IV for ~3–5 days until clinical improvement (afebrile, less pain, better function — a ≥ 50% fall in CRP where measurable supports the switch), then complete the course orally. Individualise longer courses for complicated cases (large abscess, septic emboli, pathological fracture).
